meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's grade changed before anyone called me?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now why was it entered at all, and what do you have?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
Kids draft in other programs and paste it in. Did you ask Owen about that before you entered the zero?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn the screen. And you haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen before you entered the zero.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A student misquotes a line. That's a mistake, not misconduct. Put both of these in writing for me, and still tell me whether you spoke to Owen first.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's what revising is. Hand me both documents, and I'll read them myself.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Fine, you spoke to him. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot freezes, and that's a note in your handwriting, not a document I can check. What do you propose, then?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom and a week at home are different conditions. That's your fifth point, and you still haven't answered me: what are you proposing, and what goes on his record?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because a machine's guess is worth nothing. That's twice you haven't answered me: what are you proposing, and is anything on his record right now?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

Okay. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything, but it's private, not in front of his class, and the no-record promise comes to me in writing tonight. The apology about the gradebook goes in that email too.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Okay. Tonight, in writing, with the rewrite date in the same email. And the zero comes off the gradebook until then.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Send me two days in the email and I'll confirm one with Owen. Ten minutes.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes, plus the zero off the gradebook until then and the apology in that same email. Okay.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Not today. Whatever else I have goes in my email, and I'll expect yours tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on Owen's record, confirmed in writing from you tonight. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook until the rewrite, the apology for how Owen found out, and the rewrite date in that same email. I expect your answer in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite that replaces the zero, with nothing on his record and the promise in writing tonight, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook until then, the apology and a rewrite date; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You put dated documents in front of her one at a time, each one something she could check herself, so she had nothing to wave away.
What cost ground: You let her question about whether you had spoken to Owen sit unanswered for two turns, which made her shorter and harder before you gave the November 2 conversation.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its late-night times on October 28, the night before the essay was due, came close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether you had spoken to Owen before entering the zero, lead with your November 2 conversation and the note you wrote that day, so your answer comes before her second ask.
